united-states/alexandria-lakes.text: Minnesota's first American Viticultural Area, in Douglas County, ringed by six freshwater lakes. It covers about 10,880 acres in a cold plant hardiness zone of 4a to 4b. Minnesota's most planted grapes are cold-hardy varieties such as Frontenac, Marquette and La Crescent.

united-states/altus.text: Arkansas's first AVA, in the Arkansas River Valley around the town of Altus. The soils are fine to gravelly, sandy to silty loam, and slightly to strongly acidic. It sits inside the Arkansas Mountain and Ozark Mountain AVAs, and five wineries worked in the area as of 2008.

united-states/appalachian-high-country.text: A high-elevation AVA of about 1.5 million acres, mainly in North Carolina with parts in Tennessee and Virginia. It was created in 2016 so growers could label wines made primarily from grapes grown across eight counties in the Appalachian mountains.

united-states/arizona.text: A state with three wine regions: Sonoita, Willcox and Verde Valley. Most vineyards are in the southeast, south and east of Tucson. Arizona has had success with grape varieties native to Italy and the Rhône Valley of southern France.

united-states/arkansas.text: A state that makes wine from European varieties such as Cabernet Sauvignon, Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Riesling, and from native grapes such as Cynthiana and Muscadine. The multi-state Ozark Mountain AVA reaches into it.

united-states/arkansas-mountain.text: An AVA in the Ozark Mountains of Arkansas, split by the Arkansas River. It sits inside the multi-state Ozark Mountain AVA and contains the smaller Altus AVA, which shares its terroir. It was created in 1986 on a petition from Wiederkehr Wine Cellars.

united-states/augusta.text: The first AVA created in the United States, in 1980, in the Missouri Rhineland. It covers 9,600 acres around the town of Augusta in St Charles County, about 40 miles west of St Louis. Missouri's most planted grapes are Norton, Vignoles and Chambourcin.

united-states/bell-mountain.text: A tiny Texas Hill Country AVA of 3,200 acres on the slopes of Bell Mountain, north of Fredericksburg. It was the first AVA wholly inside Texas. It sits on the northern rim of the Edwards Plateau, and its last winery had closed by 2025.

united-states/cape-may-peninsula.text: A New Jersey AVA at the state's southern tip, set within the Outer Coastal Plain AVA. Sandy or sandy loam soils drain well, and the Atlantic Ocean and Delaware Bay moderate the climate, giving a more moderate temperature range and a longer growing season.

united-states/catoctin.text: A Maryland AVA of about 169,600 acres in Frederick and Washington counties, west of the town of Frederick. It takes in an intermountain valley and the uplands around it, bounded by Catoctin Mountain and South Mountain. The name means "speckled rock".

united-states/central-delaware-valley.text: A multi-state AVA along the Delaware River between Trenton, New Jersey, and Easton, Pennsylvania. It covers about 96,000 acres in Hunterdon and Mercer counties in New Jersey and Bucks County in Pennsylvania, and was New Jersey's first AVA.

united-states/colorado.text: A state whose vineyards lie mostly on the western slope of the Rocky Mountains, with more wineries along the Front Range. Its most planted grapes are Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Riesling and Chardonnay. Its AVAs are Grand Valley and West Elks.

united-states/connecticut.text: A state whose modern wine industry began with the Connecticut Winery Act in 1978. It has three AVAs. The coast and Connecticut River valley are warmer than the highlands to the east and west.

united-states/crest-of-the-blue-ridge-he.text: A North Carolina AVA covering 215 square miles in Henderson County, created in 2019. It had 14 commercial vineyards on about 70 acres and two wineries. Its distinguishing features are its climate and topography, above all its elevation.

wiki.title: Crest of the Blue Ridge Henderson County AVA

united-states/cumberland-valley.text: A two-state AVA in a valley about 80 miles long, running from the Potomac River in Maryland toward the Susquehanna River in Pennsylvania. South Mountain, the northern end of the Blue Ridge, borders it on the southeast and the Allegheny Mountains on the northwest.

united-states/dahlonega-plateau.text: A Georgia AVA on the northeastern part of the Dahlonega Plateau, in the northern foothills of the Georgia Piedmont. It covers parts of Lumpkin and White counties, and was Georgia's second AVA, created in 2018.

united-states/eagle-foothills.text: An Idaho AVA northwest of Boise and the first sub-appellation of the Snake River Valley AVA. Elevations run from 2,490 to 3,412 feet, with vineyards below 3,000 feet. The climate is cool, and most vines are at one vineyard in the center.

united-states/eastern-connecticut-highla.text: A Connecticut AVA covering the eastern third of the state, about 797,000 acres of rolling hills at 200 to 1,000 feet. It was created in 2019 and began with 16 commercial vineyards on about 115 acres and six bonded wineries.

united-states/escondido-valley.text: A small AVA of about 32,000 acres in Pecos County, in the Trans-Pecos region of west Texas. It had one winery, with about 250 acres of vines. That winery went bankrupt in 2022, and its vineyards were abandoned.

united-states/fennville.text: Michigan's first AVA, in Allegan County in the southwest, set within the Lake Michigan Shore AVA. It was created on a petition from Fenn Valley Vineyards.

united-states/fredericksburg-in-the-texa.text: A Texas AVA of 70,400 acres around the town of Fredericksburg in Gillespie County, within the Texas Hill Country AVA. It began with about eight vineyards on 50 acres, and the area also had many commercial peach growers.

wiki.title: Fredericksburg in the Texas Hill Country AVA

united-states/georgia.text: A US state with two AVAs, Upper Hiwassee Highlands and Dahlonega Plateau. Wine is made in all fifty states, and the American industry rests almost entirely on the European Vitis vinifera.

united-states/grand-valley.text: A high-altitude river valley AVA in Mesa County, Colorado, around Grand Junction between Palisade and Fruita. Its 75,990 acres average 4,000 to 5,000 feet in elevation and are irrigated by canals. It was Colorado's first AVA.

united-states/haw-river-valley.text: A North Carolina AVA of 868 square miles in the north-central part of the state, centered on Burlington and cut by the Haw River. It lies between Greensboro and Durham-Raleigh, and was created in 2009.

united-states/hawaii.text: A state whose wine is made mainly on Maui, with some on the island of Hawaii, and is largely fruit wine such as pineapple sparkling wine. Its first vineyard dates to 1815. Ulupalakua, on Maui, is its only AVA.

united-states/hermann.text: A Missouri AVA on the southern bank of the Missouri River, named for the town of Hermann. Many of its roughly 200 acres of vines are on south-facing slopes. Stone Hill Winery is based in Hermann.

united-states/idaho.text: A state whose vineyards date to the 1860s, before those of Washington and Oregon, until Prohibition crippled them. Grapes were replanted in the 1970s in the Snake River Valley. Its AVAs are Snake River Valley and Lewis-Clark Valley.

united-states/illinois.text: A state whose first AVA, Shawnee Hills, was named in 2006. Its other AVA is the huge Upper Mississippi River Valley. The most planted grapes are Chambourcin, Norton and Maréchal Foch.

united-states/indiana.text: A state with two AVAs, the multi-state Ohio River Valley and the Indiana Uplands. Its most planted grapes are Traminette, Chambourcin and Chardonel.

united-states/indiana-uplands.text: An AVA covering much of the Indiana Uplands in south-central Indiana. It borders the Ohio River Valley AVA, whose boundary was cut back to avoid an overlap. It started with 19 vineyards on about 200 acres and 17 wineries.

united-states/iowa.text: A state that was once among the largest wine producers, until Prohibition. Very warm summer days and extremely cold winter nights are hard on vines, so most vineyards focus on French hybrid and native American grapes, led by Marquette, Frontenac and La Crosse. Loess Hills District is its western AVA.

united-states/kanawha-river-valley.text: A West Virginia AVA of 640,000 acres in the Kanawha River watershed, near Charleston. It lies wholly within the state and is a sub-appellation of the Ohio River Valley AVA.

united-states/lake-michigan-shore.text: A Michigan AVA in the southwest corner of the state, bordered by Lake Michigan. It covers 1.28 million acres and is known as a fruit belt.

united-states/lake-wisconsin.text: Wisconsin's first AVA, in Columbia and Dane counties, with the Wisconsin River and Lake Wisconsin on its borders. Most vines sit at 800 to 900 feet on glacial gravel and sandy loam, and French hybrid grapes have had the most success.

united-states/lancaster-valley.text: Pennsylvania's first AVA, in Lancaster and Chester counties around the city of Lancaster. The valley is about 31 miles long and 12 wide and covers 225,000 acres, with about 400 acres under vine. Climate was not a factor in setting its boundary.

united-states/leelanau-peninsula.text: A Michigan AVA on a 330-square-mile peninsula between Lake Michigan and Grand Traverse Bay. The lake effect moderates temperature extremes and delays budding past the late spring frosts.

united-states/lehigh-valley.text: A Pennsylvania AVA of 1.2 million acres, a long valley between Second Mountain to the north and South Mountain to the south, running from Jim Thorpe to Easton. Pennsylvania's most planted grapes are Catawba, Chambourcin, Cabernet Franc and Chardonnay.

united-states/lewis-clark-valley.text: A two-state AVA in northern Idaho and southeastern Washington, between the Clearwater and mid-Snake rivers. It covers 479 square miles with nearly 100 acres under vine, and borders the Columbia Valley AVA.

united-states/linganore.text: A Maryland AVA in Frederick and Carroll counties, east of the town of Frederick, on the Piedmont Plateau. It began with about 52 acres of commercial vines, scattered widely, which was about 19.5 percent of Maryland's grape acreage in 1980.

united-states/loess-hills-district.text: An AVA of 8.25 million acres in western Iowa and northwestern Missouri, a long strip along the Big Sioux and Missouri rivers. It began with about 66 vineyards on 112 acres supplying 13 wineries. Iowa's most planted grapes are Marquette, Frontenac and La Crosse.

united-states/loramie-creek.text: A small Ohio AVA of 3,600 acres in Shelby County, between Loramie Creek and Turtle Creek. It was once known for red wine from the French-American hybrid Baco Noir.

united-states/martha-s-vineyard.text: An AVA covering the islands of Martha's Vineyard and Chappaquiddick off the Massachusetts coast, set within Southeastern New England. Its 1985 creation was contested by a Napa Valley vineyard of the same name. The maritime location gives a slightly warmer climate and a growing season almost three weeks longer than nearby coastal Massachusetts.

united-states/maryland.text: A state whose wine industry grew from its first bonded winery, Boordy Vineyards, which opened in 1945. Its AVAs include Cumberland Valley, Catoctin and Linganore, and the industry is estimated to add $50 million a year to the state economy.

united-states/massachusetts.text: A state whose vineyards are mostly in the south, inside the Southeastern New England AVA. Many wineries rely on cold-hardy hybrids such as Seyval, Vidal blanc and Maréchal Foch. Martha's Vineyard has a milder climate, and Nashoba Valley is a warmer inland AVA.

united-states/mesilla-valley.text: A two-state AVA along the Rio Grande, from north of Las Cruces, New Mexico, into El Paso County, Texas. It was the first AVA in both states. The climate is dry and hot, and Cabernet Sauvignon, Zinfandel and Syrah are the most important grapes.

united-states/michigan.text: A state whose quality wine comes mostly from five AVAs: Fennville, Lake Michigan Shore, Leelanau Peninsula, Old Mission Peninsula and Tip of the Mitt. Riesling is the most planted grape, ahead of Pinot Noir and Chardonnay. It is also a leader in fruit wines such as cherry.

united-states/middle-rio-grande-valley.text: A central New Mexico AVA along the Rio Grande, centered on Albuquerque, with grape growing dating to 1629. The valley is narrow and runs from Santa Fe southward. The land rises from 4,000 to 6,500 feet, and the climate is semi-arid with warm days and cool nights.

united-states/middleburg-virginia.text: A northern Virginia Piedmont AVA in Fauquier and Loudoun counties, about 50 miles west of Washington, D.C. It is ringed by the Potomac River and several mountain ranges. Its distinguishing features are climate, topography, geology and soils.

united-states/mimbres-valley.text: A southwestern New Mexico AVA along the Mimbres River, around Deming, between Silver City and Columbus. Most vineyards lie at 4,000 to 6,000 feet, with the Mogollon Mountains to the north. It was New Mexico's second AVA.

united-states/minnesota.text: A very cold state where many vines are buried under soil for winter. It does extensive research on cold-hardy hybrids, and Frontenac, Marquette and La Crescent are the most planted. It hosts the International Cold Climate Wine Competition.

united-states/mississippi.text: A hot, humid state where European and French hybrid grapes are hard to grow. Its three commercial wineries focus almost entirely on the Muscadine grape. Its one AVA is Mississippi Delta.

united-states/mississippi-delta.text: A three-state AVA of about 3.8 million acres on the east bank of the Mississippi River between Memphis and Vicksburg, mostly in Mississippi. It is a leaf-shaped, flat alluvial plain about 180 miles long.

united-states/missouri.text: A state whose wine industry was founded by German immigrants in the 19th century, which gave its wine corridor the name Missouri Rhineland. It was the nation's second-largest producer before Prohibition. Norton, Vignoles and Chambourcin are the most planted grapes.

united-states/monticello.text: A central Virginia Piedmont AVA on the eastern slopes of the Blue Ridge, named for Thomas Jefferson's home. It includes the Southwest Mountains. About 30 varieties grow there, and the most notable are Cabernet Franc, Chardonnay and Viognier.

united-states/new-jersey.text: A state whose wine industry grew after 1981, when the legislature relaxed Prohibition-era limits. It has four AVAs: Central Delaware Valley, Warren Hills, Outer Coastal Plain and Cape May Peninsula. In 2012 it had 1,082 acres of grapes.

united-states/new-mexico.text: A state with one of the oldest wine-making traditions in the United States. Friars planted the first wine grapes in 1629 in what is now the Middle Rio Grande Valley AVA. Its AVAs are Middle Rio Grande Valley, Mesilla Valley and Mimbres Valley.

united-states/north-carolina.text: A state where growers first cultivated the native Scuppernong grape, which makes a sweet wine. Since 1972 most wine has come from Vitis vinifera, though French hybrids and Vitis labrusca remain common.

united-states/north-fork-of-roanoke.text: A Virginia AVA on the eastern slopes of the Allegheny Mountains, west of Roanoke. The valley runs 22 miles along the Roanoke River, with vineyards at 1,200 to 2,200 feet. It is named for the North Fork river.

united-states/northern-neck-george-washi.text: A Virginia AVA of 590,080 acres in five counties on the Northern Neck peninsula, between the Potomac and Rappahannock rivers in the Tidewater region. It began with sixteen vineyards on 92.5 acres.

wiki.title: Northern Neck George Washington Birthplace AVA

united-states/ohio.text: A state whose wine was historically made from native grapes such as Vitis labrusca, though hybrids and vinifera are now common. It had 280 commercial wineries in 2018. Riesling and Vidal are the most planted grapes.

united-states/ohio-river-valley.text: One of the largest AVAs in the country, along the Ohio River through Indiana, Kentucky, Ohio and West Virginia. It was created in 1983 and was cut back in 2013 when Indiana Uplands was formed. It contains the Kanawha River Valley AVA.

united-states/old-mission-peninsula.text: A Michigan AVA on a peninsula about 19 miles long and no more than three miles wide, reaching into Grand Traverse Bay at Traverse City. It covers about 19,200 acres, with 1,800 acres of vinifera vineyards.

united-states/outer-coastal-plain.text: A New Jersey AVA of 2.25 million acres covering the state's eastern and southernmost regions, including the Atlantic coastline. It is one of five physiographic regions of New Jersey and contains the Cape May Peninsula AVA.

united-states/ozark-highlands.text: A Missouri AVA of 1.28 million acres in the Ozark Mountains, east of Jefferson City, around Rolla. It borders the Mark Twain National Forest. It was created on a petition from seven Missouri wineries and sits within Ozark Mountain.

united-states/ozark-mountain.text: A very large AVA of 35.2 million acres across northwest Arkansas, southern Missouri and northeast Oklahoma. It is one of the largest AVAs, and it contains Arkansas Mountain, Ozark Highlands and Hermann.

united-states/pennsylvania.text: A state where Catawba, Chambourcin, Cabernet Franc and Chardonnay are the most planted grapes, followed by Vidal and Merlot. Its AVAs include Lehigh Valley and Lancaster Valley.

united-states/rocky-knob.text: A Virginia AVA of 9,000 acres on the eastern slopes of the Blue Ridge, in Floyd and Patrick counties, beside the Blue Ridge Parkway. Elevations run from 1,600 to 3,574 feet. Strong winds at that height help protect grapes from fungus and mildew.

united-states/shawnee-hills.text: Illinois's first AVA, in the south of the state between the Mississippi and Ohio rivers. It covers over 2,140 square miles, about 80 miles east to west by 20 miles north to south.

united-states/shenandoah-valley.text: A Virginia and West Virginia AVA of 2.4 million acres in the valley between the Blue Ridge Mountains and the Appalachian and Allegheny Plateaus. It was Virginia's first AVA, and had about 116 acres of vines when it was created.

united-states/snake-river-valley.text: A large AVA of 8,263 square miles across southwestern Idaho and two eastern Oregon counties. Wines must use at least 85 percent grapes grown within it. It contains the Eagle Foothills AVA.

united-states/sonoita.text: Arizona's first AVA, in the southeast by the Mexican border, south of Tucson. It covers about 208,000 acres. The Babacomari Ranch worked with the University of Arizona to test Vitis vinifera and winemaking here.

united-states/southeastern-new-england.text: A vast AVA covering thirteen counties in Connecticut, Massachusetts and Rhode Island, including all coastal plain and islands within 15 miles of Long Island Sound, Cape Cod and Massachusetts Bay. It contains Martha's Vineyard.

united-states/swan-creek.text: A North Carolina AVA of 96,000 acres with 75 acres of vines, in Iredell, Wilkes and Yadkin counties. Its northern 60 percent lies inside the Yadkin Valley AVA and the rest extends south of it. It was created in 2008.

united-states/tennessee.text: A state whose wine industry was wiped out by Prohibition. The modern industry focuses on French hybrid and native grapes, which resist the fungal diseases of its humid climate. Most wineries are in Middle and East Tennessee.

united-states/texas.text: A state with a long wine history, going back to Spanish missionaries near El Paso in the 1650s. It ranked fifth in wine production in 2024, with over 9,300 acres of Vitis vinifera. Its AVAs include Texas Hill Country and Texas High Plains.

united-states/texas-davis-mountains.text: A west Texas AVA of about 270,000 acres in Jeff Davis County, surrounded by the Chihuahuan Desert and using cooler elevations. It was the last AVA recognized in the 20th century and began with one winery on about 40 acres.

united-states/texas-high-plains.text: A Texas AVA of over 8 million acres on the Llano Estacado, the second largest in the state. Vineyards sit on flat land at 3,000 to 4,000 feet, share it with cotton, sorghum and wheat, and are irrigated from the Ogallala Aquifer.

united-states/texas-hill-country.text: A Texas AVA of 9.6 million acres across the Edwards Plateau, west of the Balcones Fault. It is the state's southernmost AVA and one of the largest in the country. It contains Bell Mountain and Fredericksburg in the Texas Hill Country.

united-states/texoma.text: A north-central Texas AVA of 2.3 million acres on the south side of Lake Texoma and the Red River, on the Texas-Oklahoma line. The name blends Texas and Oklahoma. It spans parts of Montague, Cooke, Grayson and Fannin counties.

united-states/tip-of-the-mitt.text: A Michigan AVA of 1.77 million acres at the northern tip of the Lower Peninsula, north of Leelanau Peninsula and Old Mission Peninsula. Lake Michigan, Lake Huron and the Straits of Mackinac border it.

united-states/ulupalakua.text: Hawaii's first AVA, on the western slopes of Mount Haleakala on Maui. It covers about 70 acres with about 16 acres of vines, making it the nation's smallest appellation. Grapes are processed at the nearby Maui Wines facility.

united-states/upper-cumberland.text: A Middle Tennessee AVA of about 2.18 million acres in eight counties, around Cookeville and McMinnville. It was created in 2024 and has 55 vineyards on over 71 acres, supplying nine wineries.

united-states/upper-hiwassee-highlands.text: A two-state AVA near the southern end of the Blue Ridge Mountains, over parts of southwestern North Carolina and northern Georgia. It was Georgia's first AVA. It covers about 441,600 acres, with 54 acres under vine at the start.

united-states/upper-mississippi-river-va.text: The nation's largest AVA, 19.1 million acres along the Upper Mississippi River in Illinois, Iowa, Minnesota and Wisconsin. The climate is continental and cool, and rolling hills give vines maximum sun. It is 50 times larger than the Bordeaux regions of France.

united-states/verde-valley.text: A central Arizona AVA of about 130,000 acres around the Verde River, 100 miles north of Phoenix, with steep surrounding foothills. When it was approved in 2021, 24 vineyards on about 125 acres supplied eleven wineries.

united-states/virginia.text: A state whose hot, humid summers challenge growers, and whose industry only grew past novelty status in the last twenty years. Vitis vinifera is 75 percent of production. Chardonnay, Cabernet Franc and Merlot are the most planted grapes, mostly in central and northern Virginia.

united-states/virginia-peninsula.text: A southeast Virginia AVA of 673,059 acres on the landform between the York and James rivers, Hampton Roads and Chesapeake Bay. It includes Williamsburg and Hampton, and began with five vineyards on about 112 acres. It was created in 2021.

united-states/virginias-eastern-shore.text: A Virginia AVA in Accomack and Northampton counties, created in 1990.

united-states/warren-hills.text: A New Jersey AVA covering most of Warren County, in several small valleys formed by tributaries of the Delaware River. Most vineyards are on southeast-facing hillsides. It was created in 1988 on a petition from Alba Vineyard and other local growers.

united-states/west-elks.text: A Colorado AVA of 48,405 acres on mesa lands along the North Fork Gunnison River, around Paonia and Hotchkiss in Delta County. It is bordered by the West Elk Range and the higher Grand Mesa. It was Colorado's second AVA.

united-states/west-virginia.text: A state with three AVAs: Shenandoah Valley, Ohio River Valley and Kanawha River Valley. Mountain winds dry the vine canopy and reduce fungal disease. Cold winters push most producers toward French hybrid and native Vitis labrusca grapes.

united-states/western-connecticut-highla.text: A Connecticut AVA covering all of Litchfield County and parts of Fairfield, New Haven and Hartford. It has little water moderation, a cool climate and a short growing season of mid-May to mid-September. The soil is glacial schist and gneiss.

united-states/willcox.text: A southeastern Arizona AVA around the city of Willcox, mostly flat terrain over 4,000 feet, including much of the Sulphur Springs Valley. Willcox Playa, a dry ancient lake bed, is its lowest point. It was Arizona's second AVA.

united-states/wisconsin.text: A state that shares the huge Upper Mississippi Valley AVA, the nation's largest, with Minnesota, Iowa and Illinois, and wholly contains two others, Lake Wisconsin and Wisconsin Ledge. A statewide winery association promotes winemaking.

united-states/wisconsin-ledge.text: A northeast Wisconsin AVA of 2.4 million acres along the western end of the Niagara Escarpment, known locally as The Ledge. It was created in 2012.

united-states/yadkin-valley.text: North Carolina's first AVA, about 1.4 million acres in seven counties of the northwest in the Yadkin River Valley. It began with over 30 growers on about 350 acres and three wineries. Part of the Swan Creek AVA lies inside it.
